clue.text: Hesitates, but leaves to provide shelter for poor

indicators.note: the word for leaving wraps round the word for poor, giving it cover from the outside

parts.note: to leave a place is to vacate it
poor, as in poor health, means ill

explanation.surface: Someone dithers, yet still walks out of the room to arrange a roof over the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide shelter for' puts ILL inside VACATES, between VAC and ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between choices, the same as hesitating.

clue.text: Large pole kept in tub

indicators.note: the pole is held inside the container word, as something kept in a tub

parts.note: a vat is a large tub
S is the abbreviation for the south pole

explanation.surface: A big post has been stored inside a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' puts S inside VAT; 'pole' gives a compass point here, not a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast is a synonym for very large.

clue.text: Politicians coming out of the cupboard

explanation.surface: Members of parliament step out of a closet together.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests politicians coming out, but the two definitions are senior ministers and a piece of storage furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is the body of senior ministers in government, and also a cupboard with shelves or drawers.

clue.text: The star of the east?

parts.note: the star that guided the Magi in the Nativity story literally showed them the way, and the phrase also means a prominent person

explanation.surface: A question about the star seen in the east at the Nativity.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a playful reading: the Bethlehem star was a light that led the wise men.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent, influential person is called a star, and the Nativity star literally guided travellers with its glow.

clue.text: Consumed by a legal right to withdraw contact

indicators.note: by means beside here, so the word for consumed is set next to the legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement has swallowed up the right to cut off communication.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go A, LIEN, ATE, with 'by' only placing ATE alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone, cutting off friendly relations, is to alienate them.

clue.text: Turns out, but always turns inside out!

parts.note: ever is an old word for always, as in ever ready

indicators.note: read as the word turns with its inside taken out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something flips over, but in fact keeps turning itself inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside out' keeps T and S from 'turns', dropping URN. The exclamation mark flags that 'inside out' is not meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is to turn an organ or part outward, so everts means turns out.

clue.text: New money

explanation.surface: Freshly minted cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint describes something unused and pristine, and a mint is also a large sum of money.

clue.text: Transfixed, I married — and blanched

parts.note: to blanch is to go pale, so blanched means paled

explanation.surface: A newlywed reports being stunned, wedded and white as a sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced right through, which is what transfixed literally means.

clue.text: Edward puts up with children's playthings

parts.note: Teddy is a pet form of the name Edward
to put up with something is to bear it

explanation.surface: Edward tolerates kids' toys.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy bears were named after Theodore Roosevelt, but here TEDDY comes from Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed toy bears are classic toys for young ones.

clue.text: Superficially, he's hardly a sailor

parts.note: a crewman who serves beneath the waves is barely on the surface at all, so hardly a sailor in the surface sense

explanation.surface: Judged at a glance, this man is scarcely a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superficially' looks like 'on a quick look', but means 'at the surface of the sea', where this sailor rarely is.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew member of an undersea vessel is a sailor who spends his time below the surface.

clue.text: Hurried exercises in borders of Scotland

indicators.note: the exercises sit inside the letters taken from the edges of Scotland
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone rushed through workouts along the Scottish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders of' gives S and D, the first and last letters of Scotland; 'in' puts PE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, meaning moved quickly or rushed.

clue.text: Foie gras farm producing cheese

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the given letters, here a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A farm making foie gras turns out dairy products as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges the letters of FOIE GRAS FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Fromage frais is a soft fresh French dairy product, a type of fresh curd cheese.

clue.text: A collection of books one is against

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who owns a book collection is opposed to something.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning opposed to.

clue.text: Of course aunt's upset — come round!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of aunt are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word aunt, with the 's read as a link
to rally is to recover or come round after illness

explanation.surface: Of course Auntie is cross; do pay her a visit!
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AUNT into NATU; RALLY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally is used as an interjection meaning obviously or certainly.

clue.text: Shopping centre on Sunday — picture the conditions to be enforced!

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the abbreviation for Sunday sits at the top

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre
a print is a picture made by printing, such as an engraving

explanation.surface: An instruction about Sunday trading, with a picture of the rules to be imposed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts S above MALL; PRINT completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the detailed terms and conditions in a contract, often in tiny type.

clue.text: Moderate attendance after a couple of notes

indicators.note: after places the attendance word behind the two notes

parts.note: mi and ti are two notes of the sol-fa scale
the gate is the number of spectators attending a sporting event

explanation.surface: Turnout eased following a couple of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to lessen or soften, the verb sense of moderate.

clue.text: Muse about director-general's strange blemish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled muse goes around the abbreviation
strange means odd or unusual, signalling that the letters of muse are rearranged

parts.note: DG is the abbreviation for director-general

explanation.surface: A muse hovers around a BBC chief's odd stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges MUSE into SMUE, and 'about' wraps it round DG. DG is familiar from the BBC's Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge is a smear or stain, a kind of blemish.

clue.text: Match eagle perhaps, and grouse

parts.note: a game is a match, as in a game of tennis
an eagle is an example of a bird

explanation.surface: A golf match featuring an eagle, with a complaint to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like a verb meaning complain, and 'eagle' suggests golf; both are birds here.
explanation.definitionFit: Grouse are shot for sport and food, the classic example of a hunted fowl.

clue.text: One politician protected by cover, it's clear

indicators.note: protected by means the cover encloses the other letters

parts.note: a lid is a cover
I is the Roman numeral for one
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A lone politician is shielded by a cover story, it's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts I and MP inside LID.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid describes water or glass that is transparent, perfectly see-through.

clue.text: Performing shortly after the first of may in heavy rain

indicators.note: after sets the following pieces behind the opening letter
the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a performer on stage is on
soon means shortly

explanation.surface: A show soon after the first of May, held in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' is printed lowercase so it reads as the month; only its first letter, M, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The monsoon is the seasonal wind in South Asia that brings torrential downpours.

clue.text: The effect of gin, initially in German town

definitions.text: The effect of gin, initially in German town

indicators.note: the first letter of gin goes inside the name of the town

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Germany

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking just the opening letter

explanation.surface: Too much spirit consumed on a night out in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes G from 'gin', and 'in' places it inside HANOVER. The whole clue also describes the morning-after feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the headache and nausea after drinking too much alcohol.

clue.text: The flavour given by a new occupant of house

indicators.note: an occupant lives inside, so these letters go within the house word

parts.note: a villa is a house

explanation.surface: A new tenant of the home brings a particular taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupant of' puts A and N inside VILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is a flavouring from orchid pods, used in ice cream and baking.

clue.text: Burrow out of half-Nelson, under barrel

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so the barrel comes first

parts.note: a tun is a large barrel or cask

indicators.note: half of a word here means its first half

explanation.surface: Escape from a wrestling hold beneath a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-Nelson is a wrestling hold; here 'half' takes NEL from Nelson, set under TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunnel is an underground passage, like the burrow a mole digs.

clue.text: Hope tunes are played in a flat

indicators.note: tunes are played, and that playing reworks the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Musical hopes are performed in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are played' rearranges the letters of HOPE TUNES.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is a luxury apartment on the top floor of a building.

clue.text: Supply amusement on the day

parts.note: fun means amusement

explanation.surface: Providing entertainment on the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something is to provide the money for it, a sense of supply.

clue.text: Defeated general kept the advantage

indicators.note: kept means held within, so the answer sits inside the words Defeated general

explanation.surface: A beaten commander still held the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept' marks the run spanning the end of 'Defeated' and the start of 'general'.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is an advantage, as in having the edge over a rival.

clue.text: One argument against a symbol of worship

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A single objection to a religious emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred image, especially in Orthodox churches, venerated in devotion.

clue.text: Lurid and venal display that's incomparable

indicators.note: display means show off, laying out the letters in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A garish and corrupt show without equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' rearranges the letters of LURID and VENAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrivalled means having no equal, beyond comparison.

clue.text: Lean towards the finish in Yorkshire

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect the is shortened to t', so in Yorkshire the becomes T
end means finish

explanation.surface: Someone inclines towards the end of a Yorkshire visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Yorkshire' tells you to say 'the' as a Yorkshireman would, t', giving T before END. Yorkshire is a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend to do something is to be inclined that way.

clue.text: Bonnie's friend leads off horse

parts.note: Clyde Barrow was the partner of Bonnie Parker in the outlaw duo Bonnie and Clyde

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of leads are jumbled

explanation.surface: Bonnie's companion takes the lead on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LEADS into SDALE, following CLYDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a heavy draught breed from Scotland.
